title: Reconstruct the LSTM
summary: Follow information through the cell state and gates, then implement the nonlinearities and a complete LSTM cell.

parts.title: The constant-error path
parts.prompt: How does the additive cell-state update help gradients travel across many time steps?
parts.answer: The cell state combines a retained previous state and a new candidate additively. When the forget gate stays near one, derivatives can pass through many steps without repeated multiplication by a small recurrent weight.
hints: Differentiate c_t with respect to c_(t-1).
The forget gate controls the direct path.

parts.title: Three gates, three jobs
parts.prompt: State the roles of the forget, input, and output gates.
parts.answer: The forget gate chooses retained memory, the input gate controls writing the candidate, and the output gate selects which cell information becomes the exposed hidden state.
hints: Read, write, and erase are separate decisions.
Only one gate directly scales old memory.

parts.title: Why tanh for candidates?
parts.prompt: Why use sigmoid for gates but tanh for candidate content and exposed cell values?
parts.answer: Sigmoid produces coefficients in [0,1], suitable for gates. Tanh produces signed bounded content, allowing memory to add positive or negative evidence while limiting magnitude.
hints: A gate behaves like a soft switch.

parts.title: Implement stable sigmoid
parts.prompt: Implement the sigmoid nonlinearity used by LSTM gates.

parts.title: Implement an LSTM cell
parts.prompt: Split the affine projection into input, forget, output, and candidate gates; return the new hidden and cell states.
